harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented router-on-a-stick VLAN segmentation for node1/node2/node3's shared trunk link using an Ansible playbook run from the designated control_node (node4). node1 (VyOS) got 802.1Q sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24) via native configure/commit/save. node2 was placed on tagged VLAN 10 (enp8s0.10, 10.10.10.11/24) and node3 on tagged VLAN 20 (enp8s0.20, 10.10.20.12/24) via community.general.nmcli, each with a specific static route to the other VLAN's subnet via node1 (not a competing default route). Verified true inter-VLAN routing (not bridging) via a tcpdump capture on node1's trunk interface showing ICMP packets ingress-tagged VLAN 10 and egress re-tagged VLAN 20 (TTL decrement confirms routing hop). Bootstrapped Ansible SSH access first (created an 'antrieb' user with node4's key on node2/node3; added node4's key to VyOS user 'vyos' via native VyOS config), since no Ansible-reachable credentials pre-existed. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all four managed nodes, confirming changed boot_id/uptime and full recovery of VLAN configuration, routing, and (for node4) SSH/ansible connectivity after each restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: environment.toml defines control_node=node4, a 'trunk' L2 network (dhcp=false, egress=false) shared by node1/node2/node3, and a 'mgmt' network for control/internet access

Discovered node1 (VyOS) mgmt interface eth0 needed DHCP to settle and had no pre-authorized SSH user for node4's ansible key; node2/node3 had no 'antrieb' user matching node4's ansible.cfg remote_user

Bootstrapped SSH access for Ansible: created 'antrieb' user with sudo NOPASSWD and node4's pubkey on node2 and node3; added node4's pubkey to VyOS user 'vyos' via native `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys`, then commit/save
Wrote /root/vlan-segmentation/inventory.ini and playbook.yml on node4 (the control_node), with per-host vars for vlan_id/vlan_ip/vlan_gw/peer_subnet

Playbook play 1 (host: vyos/node1): configured eth1 vif 10 (10.10.10.1/24) and vif 20 (10.10.20.1/24) via VyOS configure/commit/save, wrapped per the vyos-reference bash -c envelope using real newlines (not && chaining) so VyOS's 'configure'/'set' aliases expand correctly

Playbook play 2 (hosts: node2, node3): used community.general.nmcli to disable L3 addressing on the raw trunk NIC (enp8s0) and create tagged VLAN sub-interfaces (enp8s0.10 / enp8s0.20) with static IPs and a specific route to the peer VLAN subnet via node1 (avoided gw4/default-route conflicts with the existing lower-metric mgmt default route)
Ran the playbook via ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini playbook.yml from node4, confirmed idempotent output and correct addressing/routes on all three nodes

Verified end-to-end connectivity: node2 <-> node3 ping succeeds with TTL=63 (one router hop) via node1's 10.10.10.1/10.10.20.1 gateways; ip route get confirms per-host static routes are used, not the mgmt default route

Captured tcpdump -e vlan on node1's eth1 during a node2->node3 ping, showing packets arrive 802.1Q-tagged VLAN 10 and are re-emitted tagged VLAN 20 (and vice versa for replies), proving real routing between VLANs through node1
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, uptime -s, interface/route state) on all four nodes before any restarts

Restarted node1 (VyOS) via `sudo -n /sbin/reboot` backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect; polled until reachable again; confirmed boot_id changed and VLAN sub-interfaces, forwarding, and node2<->node3 routing all recovered
Restarted node2 via the same pattern; confirmed boot_id changed, NetworkManager auto-activated the vlan10 connection profile on boot, and routing to node3 recovered
Restarted node3 via the same pattern; confirmed boot_id changed, vlan20 connection profile auto-activated, and routing to node2 recovered

Restarted node4 (control_node) last; confirmed boot_id changed, and post-restart verified the ansible-playbook files persisted on disk, SSH key-based access to node1/node2/node3 still worked, and a --check re-run of the playbook showed the cluster still in the desired converged state

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 separated onto VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 respectively over the shared node1/node2/node3 link
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook run output and post-restart checks show node2's enp8s0.10 at 10.10.10.11/24 (VLAN 10) and node3's enp8s0.20 at 10.10.20.12/24 (VLAN 20), both tagged sub-interfaces of the shared trunk NIC enp8s0.

evidence.requirement: Traffic between node2 and node3 is routed through node1, not bridged
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1's trunk interface (eth1) shows ICMP packets between node2 and node3 arriving 802.1Q-tagged VLAN 10 and being re-emitted tagged VLAN 20 (and reverse for replies); pings between node2 and node3 succeed with TTL=63, confirming one routed hop via node1's 10.10.10.1/10.10.20.1 VLAN gateways.

evidence.requirement: Implemented using Ansible from the designated control_node
evidence.summary: ansible-playbook run from node4 (control_node per environment.toml) applied VyOS vif configuration to node1 via ansible.builtin.raw and VLAN interfaces to node2/node3 via community.general.nmcli, all tasks reporting ok/changed with no failures.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9028a473... captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-restart boot_id 16d68659... (changed) with fresh uptime; eth1.10/eth1.20 addresses, ip_forward=1, and node2->node3 routed ping all confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4d340bf4... captured; reboot ack returned before disconnect; post-restart boot_id 6a31b015... (changed); enp8s0.10 VLAN interface, NetworkManager connection profile, static route, and ping to node3 all confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id cce73776... captured; reboot ack returned before disconnect; post-restart boot_id f6ca407d... (changed); enp8s0.20 VLAN interface, static route, and ping to node2 all confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: node4 (control_node) mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a6937a34... captured; reboot ack returned before disconnect; post-restart boot_id b3be6598... (changed); ansible project files persisted on disk, SSH key access to node1/node2/node3 still functional, and a --check re-run of the playbook confirmed the managed cluster remains in its converged VLAN-segmented state.
